items.text: The  water  cycle,  also  known  as  the  hydrological  cycle,  is  a continuous process that circulates water throughout the Earth's systems.  It  involves  the  movement of water between the (548) _______,the  water  bodies  and  the  land.  The  cycle  consists  of several  key  stages,  each  playing  a  crucial  role  in  maintaining Earth's  water  balance.  At  the  heart  of  the  water  cycle  is  the process of (549)_______.This is where water from oceans, lakes and rivers is heated by the sun and turns into water vapour. This water vapour then rises into the atmosphere, where it cools and condenses  to  form  clouds.  When  these  clouds  become  heavy enough,  they  release  their  moisture through (550)_______,which can fall as rain or other forms of precipitation.

items.text:
When precipitation falls onto the land, it can take different paths. Some of it may evaporate back into the air, while some may be taken  up  by  plants  and  released  back  into  the  atmosphere through a process called (551)_______.The rest of the water may flow over the land's surface, gathering in streams and rivers that eventually lead back to the oceans, completing the cycle.
The water cycle is essential for maintaining Earth's ecosystems and  supporting  life.  It  helps  distribute  fresh  water  to  various regions, replenishes water sources, and plays a role in regulating(552)_______temperatures. Understanding  the  water cycle  is  crucial  for  addressing  water  scarcity  and  managing natural resources effectively.
Q.548. (a) environment (b) atmosphere (c) forest (d) ecosystem

Smoking  is  the  leading  cause  of  death  from  bronchogenic carcinoma of the lungs, as well as a cause of death from larynx, oral  cavity,  oesophagus,  bladder,  kidney,  pancreas,  stomach, uterine cervix and  coronary  heart  disease.  Nicotine  is  the (553)_______ addictive component  of tobacco smoke.  The additives,  too,  cause  (554)_______  to  the  body;  for  example, ammonia  can  result  in  a  100-fold  increase  in  nicotine's  (555) ______  to  enter  the  nose.  Nicotine's  'kick'  can  be  amplified  by levulinic  acid,  an  additive  used  to  conceal  the  nicotine's  harsh taste, by (556)________ the binding of nicotine to brain receptors. More  than  four  thousand  compounds  and  more  than  forty known  carcinogens  are  found  in  cigarette  smoke.  Tobacco smoke  has  been  well  (557)______  as  a  proven  carcinogen  and cancer cause for many years.
Cloze Test

Can we see (563)_______the earth is a globe? Yes, we can, when we watch a ship that sails out to sea. If we watch closely, we see that the ship begins (564)_______.The bottom  of  the  ship disappears  first,  and  then  the  ship  seems  to  sink  lower  and lower, (565)________we can only see the top of the ship, and then we see nothing at all. What is hiding the ship from us? It is the earth.  Stick  a  pin  most  of  the  way  into  an  orange,  and  (566) _______turn  the  orange  away  from  you.  You  will  see  the  pin disappear, (567)_______a ship does on the earth.
- Q.563. (a) where      (b) that        (c) if
- (d) whether
- Q.564. (a) to disappear
- (b) being disappeared
- (c) to have disappeared
- (d) to be disappeared
- Q.565.

items.text:
The silk routes are a good example of vibrant pre-modern trade and cultural links between ____(568)____ parts of the world. The name  'silk  routes'  points  to  the  ____(569)____  of  Westbound Chinese silk cargoes along this route. Historians have identified several  silk  routes,  over  land  and by sea, knitting together vast regions of Asia, and ____(570)____ Asia with Europe and northern Africa. They are known  to have  existed  since  before  the Christian  Era  and ____(571)____ almost till the fifteenth century. But  Chinese  pottery  also  _______(572)_____  the  same  route,  as did textiles and spices from India and Southeast Asia.
Q.568. (a) indifferent  (b) distant  (c) indirect   (d) further
